Accessing Variables and Results

After solving a power flow, you need to extract results. Powerful.jl provides a generic variable access API that works consistently across all models.

The Generic Access Pattern

value = get_var(solution, :ModelName, :variable, external_key)
  • solution: A PowerFlowSolution or MultiIslandSolution
  • ModelName: Symbol for model type (:Bus, :Branch, :PV, etc.)
  • variable: Symbol for variable name (:v, :theta, :p, etc.)
  • external_key: Bus number or composite key from your data file

Basic Examples

Bus Variables

using Powerful, PowerFlowData

case = PowerFlowData.parse_network("cases/ieee14.raw")
sys = SystemModel(case)
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())

# Get voltage magnitude at bus 1
v1 = get_var(sol, :Bus, :v, 1)
println("Bus 1 voltage: $v1 pu")

# Get voltage angle at bus 14
θ14 = get_var(sol, :Bus, :theta, 14)
println("Bus 14 angle: $(rad2deg(θ14))°")

# Get active power injection at bus 2
p2 = get_var(sol, :Bus, :p, 2)
println("Bus 2 net injection: $p2 pu")

Branch Variables

Branches use composite keys: (from_bus, to_bus, circuit_id)

# Branch from bus 1 to bus 2, circuit "1"
key = (1, 2, "1")

# Active power flow from bus 1
p_from = get_var(sol, :Branch, :p_i, key)

# Active power flow to bus 2
p_to = get_var(sol, :Branch, :p_j, key)

# Check power loss
loss = p_from + p_to  # Should be small positive (losses)
println("Branch loss: $loss pu")

Load and Generator Variables

PQ loads and PV generators use (bus_number, id) keys:

# PQ load at bus 3, id "1"
p_load = get_var(sol, :PQ, :p, (3, "1"))
q_load = get_var(sol, :PQ, :q, (3, "1"))

# PV generator at bus 2, id "1"
p_gen = get_var(sol, :PV, :p, (2, "1"))
v_setpoint = get_var(sol, :PV, :v0, (2, "1"))

Getting All Variables

Vectors (Internal Order)

Get all values for a variable across all instances:

# All bus voltages (in internal order)
all_voltages = get_all_vars(sol, :Bus, :v)
println("Voltages: $all_voltages")

# All branch power flows
all_flows = get_all_vars(sol, :Branch, :p_i)

Note: Results are in internal order (how they're stored in memory), not external bus number order.

Dictionaries (External Keys)

Get all values keyed by external identifiers:

# Dictionary: bus_number => voltage
v_dict = get_vars_dict(sol, :Bus, :v)
println("Bus 1 voltage: $(v_dict[1])")
println("Bus 14 voltage: $(v_dict[14])")

# Iterate in external key order
for (bus_num, voltage) in sort(collect(v_dict))
    println("Bus $bus_num: $voltage pu")
end

Working with Reports

Automatic Unit Conversion

using DataFrames

# Collect bus results (converts pu → physical units)
bus_table = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)
df = DataFrame(bus_table)

# Columns include:
# - bus_i (bus number)
# - v (voltage in kV, not pu)
# - theta (angle in degrees, not radians)
# - p, q (power in MW/MVAR, not pu)

Customizing Reports

# Only include specific variables
config = ReportConfig(
    columns = ColumnPreferences(
        include_vars = [:v, :theta]  # Only voltage and angle
    )
)
bus_table = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus; config=config)

# Exclude certain outputs
config = ReportConfig(
    columns = ColumnPreferences(
        exclude_vars = [:q]  # Hide reactive power
    )
)
bus_table = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus; config=config)

See Report Customization for more details.

Multi-Island Solutions

Multi-island systems are solved automatically with transparent variable access.

Automatic Approach (Recommended)

# Auto-detect and solve islands
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)  # Detects islands automatically
sol = solve(prob, NewtonRaphson())

# Access variables transparently - no need to track which island
v1 = get_var(sol, :Bus, :v, (1,))      # Finds bus 1 automatically
θ8 = get_var(sol, :Bus, :theta, (8,))  # Finds bus 8 automatically

# Collect all voltages across all islands
all_v = get_all_vars(sol, :Bus, :v)

# Get dictionary of all voltages
v_dict = get_vars_dict(sol, :Bus, :v)

MultiIslandSolution provides the same accessor API as PowerFlowSolution, with automatic island lookup.

Manual Approach

For explicit control over individual islands:

# Manually split and solve
result = split_islands(sys)

if result isa Vector{SystemModel}
    islands = result

    # Solve each island separately
    solutions = [solve(ACPowerFlowProblem(island), NewtonRaphson())
                 for island in islands]

    # Access from specific island solutions
    v1 = get_var(solutions[1], :Bus, :v, (1,))
    θ8 = get_var(solutions[2], :Bus, :theta, (8,))

    # Manually collect all voltages
    all_v = vcat([get_all_vars(sol, :Bus, :v) for sol in solutions]...)
end

See Multi-Island Systems for details.

Advanced: Direct Index Access

For performance-critical code, bypass external key lookup:

# Get internal index first
bus_idx = sys.order.indices[:Bus][1]  # External bus 1 → internal index

# Direct access (faster, no lookup)
v = get_var_by_index(sol, :Bus, :v, bus_idx)

Use case: Tight loops where you already know internal indices.

Common Patterns

Voltage Profile Analysis

# Get all voltages
v_dict = get_vars_dict(sol, :Bus, :v)

# Find violations
for (bus_id, v) in v_dict
    if v < 0.95 || v > 1.05
        @warn "Bus $bus_id voltage violation: $v pu"
    end
end

# Find min/max
min_v, min_bus = findmin(v_dict)
max_v, max_bus = findmax(v_dict)
println("Lowest voltage: $min_v pu at bus $min_bus")
println("Highest voltage: $max_v pu at bus $max_bus")

Power Flow Visualization

using Plots

# Get all angles
θ_dict = get_vars_dict(sol, :Bus, :theta)
bus_nums = sort(collect(keys(θ_dict)))
angles_deg = [rad2deg(θ_dict[b]) for b in bus_nums]

# Plot voltage profile
plot(bus_nums, angles_deg,
     xlabel="Bus Number",
     ylabel="Angle (degrees)",
     marker=:circle,
     legend=false)

Branch Loading Analysis

# Analyze all branches
branch_model = sys.models[:Branch]

for i in 1:length(branch_model)
    from_bus = branch_model.i[i]
    to_bus = branch_model.j[i]
    ckt = branch_model.ckt[i]

    key = (from_bus, to_bus, ckt)
    p_flow = get_var(sol, :Branch, :p_i, key)

    # Compare to rating (if available)
    if hasfield(typeof(branch_model), :rate_a)
        rating = branch_model.rate_a[i]
        loading = abs(p_flow) / rating * 100
        if loading > 100
            @warn "Branch $from_bus-$to_bus-$ckt overloaded: $(loading)%"
        end
    end
end

Available Variables by Model

Bus

  • :v - Voltage magnitude (pu)
  • :theta - Voltage angle (radians)
  • :p - Net active power injection (pu)
  • :q - Net reactive power injection (pu)

Branch

  • :p_i, :q_i - Power flow from bus i (pu)
  • :p_j, :q_j - Power flow to bus j (pu)
  • :p_loss, :q_loss - Power losses (opt-in, see reports guide)

PQ Load

  • :p, :q - Active/reactive power consumption (pu)
  • :v - Bus voltage (reference to Bus)

PV Generator

  • :p - Active power generation (pu)
  • :q - Reactive power generation (pu)
  • :v - Bus voltage (reference to Bus)
  • :v0 - Voltage setpoint (pu)

Shunt

  • :b - Susceptance (pu)
  • :g - Conductance (pu)

Tip: Use get_available_outputs(ModelType) to discover all possible outputs:

julia> get_available_outputs(Branch)
6-element Vector{Symbol}:
 :p_i
 :q_i
 :p_j
 :q_j
 :p_loss
 :q_loss

Error Handling

Key Not Found

try
    v = get_var(sol, :Bus, :v, 9999)  # Bus doesn't exist
catch e
    if e isa KeyError
        println("Bus 9999 not found in system")
    end
end

Model Not Found

# Check if model exists
if haskey(sys.models, :Transformer)
    # Access transformer variables
else
    @warn "No transformers in this system"
end
